> Quick answers up front:
> - Yes, the private control plane supports SAML for authentication and a SCIM v2 endpoint for provisioning. We recommend pushing groups via SCIM and using SAML assertions for session attributes.

Thanks — adding the detailed mapping and a few gotchas below. I've attached two files (scim-attribute-mapping.csv and saml-assertion-spec.md) for your engineers.

Summary (recommended model) — on‑prem control plane:
- Provisioning model: SCIM authoritative for groups + group->role binding. SCIM PATCH events create or update group membership; our service maps SCIM groups to RBAC roles in the control plane.
- Auth model: SAML IdP does authentication; SAML assertion must include: name, email, subject (transient is fine), and groups claim (multivalued). We also accept an explicit entitlement claim (entitlements[]) for feature flags.
- Default role mappings (example):
  * acme_admins (SCIM group) -> role: platform_admin (full control)
  * acme_ops -> role: operator (deploy/run access)
  * acme_viewers -> role: viewer (read-only)

SCIM details:
- Schema: SCIM v2 core users + groups. We require group.members.value == externalId (user id in your IdP) for reliable mapping.
- Sync pattern: push (Okta->Redwood) via TLS mutual auth. We support incremental PATCH and full sync.

KMS/HSM notes:
- If you want the control plane to use a customer HSM for key wrapping, we need:
  1) Network ACL allowing outbound to your HSM endpoint from the control plane's management VMs (we can document CIDR ranges).
  2) A certificate trust chain and PKCS#11 (or cloud KMS API) credentials.
  3) A brief key rotation handshake window during cutover (we coordinate with PS).

Audit/export:
- Preferred: push to an S3-compatible bucket in your VPC with server-side encryption using your CMK. We can also stream logs (syslog/HTTP) to your SIEM over HTTPS with mTLS.
- We sign each audit bundle and keep an index for fast repro queries. If you need longer-term immutability we can add WORM storage (extra fee).

Known constraints / gotchas:
- Group cardinality: extremely large groups (100k+) will require batching; recommend breaking into service groups.
- SCIM "displayName" collisions: we recommend relying on externalId for identity.
- If you plan to federate multiple IdPs, we need a canonical principal mapping strategy (we can accept email as canonical if consistent).

Attachments: scim-attribute-mapping.csv (example rows: scim:groups -> controlplane:role), saml-assertion-spec.md (exact attribute names and XML example).

I'll be on the call Wed 6/30 at 11am PT to walk through the CSV and sample assertions.
